name: Cambricon MLU370 (Siyuan 370) AIDC accelerators
memory_bandwidth_basis: Vendor-published for the S4/S8 card: 307.2 GB/s on LPDDR5. Cambricon states memory bandwidth is 3x the previous generation and 1.5x the energy efficiency of GDDR6, but gives no bus width or pin speed, so the figure cannot be re-derived.
notes: THE HIERARCHY POINT, and the reason this part is in a memory-bound inference study at all: MLU370 is LPDDR5 with NO HBM. At 48 GB and 307.2 GB/s the arithmetic intensity ceiling is 234 FLOP/byte even at INT8, which is roughly a third of what a same-generation HBM GPU offers. So the roofline for this part sits far left of every other record here: weight streaming dominates, the usable batch size for large models is small, and the part is realistically a high-density inference card (S4 is half-height, half-length, single-slot, 75 W passive, designed for maximum cards per server) rather than a large-model serving part. The die-level 256 TOPS INT8 quoted by the chip overview is a die figure for the 2-chiplet configuration and is 2x the S4/S8 card number, so card and die figures must not be compared. Variants: S4/S8 are inference-oriented (192 TOPS INT8 card); X4 and X8 are dual-die train+infer parts using MLU-Link. The INT4 row is flagged vendor_claim false: the vendor lists INT4 as a supported precision but publishes no separate INT4 throughput, so the 192 TOPS INT8 figure is carried over as an upper bound and must not be read as an INT4 measurement. MLU-Link provides 200 GB/s of chip-to-chip bandwidth per chip - respectable relative to its HBM-less position, and the ratio of scale-up to local bandwidth is inverted versus GPUs. Software is NeuWare plus the MagicMind MLIR-based inference engine, integrated with PyTorch and TensorFlow.
